generation.scope: For a unique integral triple octic, if the sextic double-point series gives the indicated complete rational or genus-one cofactor curve, all actual opposite matrices are recovered from square roots of its polarization and adjugate division. There are at most 1, 4, 3, or 2 nontrivial choices for the rational sextic, smooth, nodal, or cuspidal elliptic octic respectively. The generic trisecant source satisfies the seven-sextic condition and has a unique nontrivial square matrix. The smooth elliptic case gives a quartic pencil with at least three nonzero reconstructed quadratic matrices when one opposite exists.

open_mathematics: Analyze the existence and regularity of the eight-cofactor elliptic candidates, distinguish complete and deficient cofactor series including higher-dimensional images, and continue other finite-window coverage.
